title: A $250 charge replaced the required calculation on some late tax claims

beats.text: In 2017, state reviewers found exemption forms without a recorded receipt date.
That made it difficult to tell whether the claims were timely.

visual.line: That made it difficult to tell whether the claims were timely

beats.text: The next survey examined the 2020–21 assessment roll.
Some late claims received a full exemption.

visual.line: Some late claims received a full exemption

beats.text: Other properties had $250 added directly to their tax bills.
The law required a calculation based on when the claim arrived.

visual.line: The law required a calculation based on when the claim arrived

beats.text: The dollar cap limited what could remain after that calculation.

visual.line: The dollar cap limited what could remain after that calculation

beats.text: Annual claims could receive a different percentage depending on the date.
That difference matters because either taxpayers or the City can bear the error.

visual.line: That difference matters because either taxpayers or the City can bear the error

beats.text: A correction register would show which bills actually changed.

visual.line: A correction register would show which bills actually changed

beats.text: The Assessor agreed and identified a limitation in the system.

visual.line: The Assessor agreed and identified a limitation in the system

beats.text: The office said it would improve its tracking.

visual.line: The office said it would improve its tracking

beats.text: The state did not publish the amount of tax to correct.

visual.line: The state did not publish the amount of tax to correct
